conventions.convention: Laplace type uses the leading term −a^{ij}∂i∂j with a smooth real symmetric positive-definite scalar principal form. The defining manifold dimension is n ≥ 2. For rank zero, the positive-definite principal form is supplied separately.
Hermitian pairings are linear in the first variable and conjugate-linear in the second. Formal adjoints satisfy ∫⟨Pu,v⟩ = ∫⟨u,P* v⟩ for compactly supported smooth sections on boundaryless manifolds.

Complex manifolds are nonempty, Hausdorff and second countable, have complex dimension m ≥ 1, and are boundaryless. Connectedness is not required. Holomorphic bundle transition matrices are holomorphic; bundle Hermitian metrics are separate smooth data.

The E-valued Dolbeault operator acts coefficientwise in holomorphic frames, raises q by one and preserves p. Its Laplacian has principal symbol |ξ^{0,1}|² times the identity. Bidegrees outside the allowed range have zero bundles.

The analytic theorems assume full AC, compactness, no boundary and real dimension n ≥ 2. Sobolev orders are nonnegative integers, and the selfadjoint realization has domain exactly H². The shifted parametrix is modulo compact operators; nonnegativity of P is not assumed.
The Green inverse vanishes on the harmonic kernel and takes values in H² intersected with its orthogonal complement; Π is the L² orthogonal projection onto that kernel.

De Rham pairings use the Riemannian density without requiring orientation. Dolbeault cohomology here is the smooth closed/exact quotient, with no sheaf comparison asserted. Green commutation identities are asserted on smooth forms.
The torus is Rⁿ/Zⁿ with its descended Euclidean metric, n ≥ 2; k is any nonnegative integer and binomial(n,k) is zero for k > n.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC. On a compact boundaryless smooth manifold of real dimension n ≥ 2, a formally symmetric smooth second-order metric-bundle operator with scalar positive-definite real principal symbol satisfies integer-order elliptic estimates: u ∈ H¹ and Pu ∈ Hᵏ imply u ∈ Hᵏ⁺² with ‖u‖Hᵏ⁺² ≤ Ck(‖Pu‖Hᵏ + ‖u‖L²). The defined Sobolev spaces are Hilbert, have smooth density, compact successive inclusions and the stated Cʳ embeddings. For sufficiently large λ > 0, P+λ:H²→L² is a bounded bijection; its inverse is compact and selfadjoint on L², bounded Hᵏ→Hᵏ⁺², and supplies two-sided parametrices modulo compact operators. P is selfadjoint with domain exactly H².

Assume AC and exactly the preceding compact, boundaryless, scalar-positive-symbol and formal-symmetry hypotheses, with dom P=H². The kernel H is finite dimensional and smooth, ran P=H⊥ is closed, and L²=H⊕⊥ran P. There is a unique linear G:L²→H²∩H⊥ satisfying PG=I−Π on L², GP=I−Π on H² and GΠ=ΠG=0. G is bounded Hᵏ→Hᵏ⁺² for every integer k≥0, compact and selfadjoint on L², and preserves smooth sections; Π is smoothing. The stated Sobolev and smooth decompositions are topological. Formal nonnegativity additionally gives nonnegative P and G.

Assume Countable Choice for density integration. A linear differential operator of order at most two between finite-rank real Euclidean or complex Hermitian bundles over a Hausdorff second-countable boundaryless smooth manifold with a positive smooth density has a unique formal adjoint of order at most two. In orthonormal frames and density coefficient γ, P* v=Σ|α|≤2(−1)^|α|γ⁻¹Dα(γaα* v). Leading coefficients transform by the stated signed fibre-adjoint rule, (P*)*=P, and P is formally symmetric exactly when P=P*.

Under Countable Choice for integration and completion, a Hermitian complex manifold of dimension m≥1 and a Hermitian holomorphic bundle carry the globally defined coefficientwise operator ∂̄E with ∂̄E²=0, its formal adjoint and their L² Hilbert structure. The Dolbeault Laplacian is formally symmetric, nonnegative, preserves each bidegree and is Laplace type with principal symbol |ξ^{0,1}|² times the identity.

Assume AC. On a compact boundaryless Riemannian manifold of real dimension at least two, the de Rham Laplacian is nonnegative and selfadjoint on H², has finite smooth degreewise kernels and gives the orthogonal smooth harmonic/exact/coexact decomposition. Harmonic forms represent real or complex de Rham classes uniquely. On a compact Hermitian complex manifold of dimension m≥1 with a finite-rank Hermitian holomorphic bundle, the analogous assertions hold for smooth E-valued Dolbeault cohomology in each bidegree. On smooth forms DG=GD, D*G=GD*, DΠ=ΠD=D*Π=ΠD*=0, and every closed u satisfies u=Πu+D(D*Gu).

seams_checked.note: Compared the countable-choice definition and AC⇒DC⇒ACω statement with their uses in the Laplace-type definition, formal-adjoint lemma, Dolbeault definition and elliptic theorem. Integration and completion explicitly inherit ACω; the analytic theorems explicitly assume full AC. No reverse implication or choice-free existence claim is attributed to these suppliers.

Compared the supplier statements with the Kähler definition's adjoint construction, the commutator lemma's F2 local-adjoint formula, and the Hodge theorem's F1/F3 and Proof 1.2/3.2. These retain the pairing convention, compact boundaryless hypotheses, full AC, scalar positive symbol, exact H² domain and smooth Green identities. The Kähler proof handles dimension zero separately and establishes real dimension 2n≥2 before invoking the analytic supplier. Its sheaf comparison is proved separately rather than attributed to this batch.
